title: Unified Payment Gateway Abstraction
business: A global e-commerce platform managing diverse regional payment providers.
problem: The checkout service was tightly coupled to specific third-party API payloads, causing cascading failures whenever a provider updated their schema or deprecated a field, leading to high maintenance overhead.
solution: By implementing an abstraction layer, the checkout service interacts only with a standardized internal interface. The implementation details of specific regional providers are encapsulated within concrete adapter classes, hiding the complexity of vendor-specific authentication and data formatting from the core business logic.
steps: Define a common PaymentProcessor interface that specifies essential methods like authorize and capture.
Create concrete adapter classes for each regional provider that implement the PaymentProcessor interface.
Inject the appropriate adapter into the checkout service at runtime using a factory pattern.
Map vendor-specific error codes to a unified internal exception hierarchy within the adapters.
outcome: The checkout service remains stable regardless of changes in external provider APIs, allowing developers to add new payment methods by simply creating a new adapter without modifying existing core logic.
limitation: Abstraction can introduce an indirection overhead that makes debugging harder because the stack trace may point to the interface rather than the specific provider logic. To check for this, developers should monitor the depth of the call stack and ensure that logging is implemented within the concrete adapters to capture provider-specific state.

questions.question: In Unified Payment Gateway Abstraction, why is an abstraction layer used to handle third-party APIs?
options: To eliminate the need for third-party payment providers entirely.
To prevent cascading failures caused by tight coupling to specific vendor API payloads.
To increase the speed of the payment processing network.
To reduce the cost of transaction fees charged by providers.
